 Oral Judgment

This appeal is preferred by the claimants against the judgment and award dated 10.11.2016 passed by the Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-VII, Vijayapura [for short 'Tribunal'], in MVC No.2165/2014, seeking enhancement of compensation.
2. One Kashinath met with an accident on 17.08.2014 and died.
His wife and children had filed claim petition claiming compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- with interest.

The Tribunal considered the entire materials on record and awarded Rs.3,93,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till realisation and directed respondent No.1 - owner of the vehicle to pay the compensation and exonerated respondent No.2 - Insurance Company from its liability.
Aggrieved by the said order, claimants filed this appeal.

3. The main contentions of the claimants are that the Tribunal erred exonerating the Insurance Company NC: 2025:KHC-K:6796 HC-KAR from its liability on the ground that the driver of the Tractor bearing its temporary registration No.MH-13/TR-B- 490 was not having valid driving license at the time of accident and directing respondent No.1 to pay the entire compensation, who remained ex-parte before the Tribunal.
It is contended that, the deceased is 3rd party and the Tribunal instead of ordering for 'pay and recover' to the Insurance Company, exonerated the Insurance Company.

It is also contended that the deceased was earning Rs.15,000/- per month, but the Tribunal has taken the income at Rs.4,000/- per month and granted meagre compensation under all heads and thus, requested for enhancement of the compensation.

4. Heard arguments of both the parties and perused the material available on record.
5.
Though it is stated that the deceased was earning Rs.15,000 per month, no document is produced to prove the same.

In the absence of proof of income, as per the chart issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services NC: 2025:KHC-K:6796 HC-KAR Authority, this Court finds it just and reasonable to take the notional income of the deceased at Rs.7,500/- per month for the accident of the year 2014.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: As the age of the deceased was 59 years at the time of accident, 10% of future prospects is to be added to Rs.7,500/- as per the law laid down by the Apex Court in the case of National Insurance CO. Ltd vs. Pranay Sethi and Others1.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Accordingly, 10% of Rs.7,500/- comes to Rs.750/- and thus,
total income would be Rs.8,250/-.
If 1/4th of this amount is deducted towards the personal expenses of the deceased, the claimants entitled for 3/4th of the income.

Thus, the loss of dependency comes to:
Rs.8,250/- x 12 x 9 x 3/4 = Rs.6,68,250/-.
6.

Further, claimant No.1 being the wife of the deceased is entitled for Rs.48,000/- towards loss of spousal consortium and claimant Nos.2 to 5 being children 2017 ACJ 2700 SC NC:
2025:KHC-K:6796 HC-KAR of the deceased are entitled for Rs.48,000/- each, for loss of parental consortium, in total Rs.2,40,000/-.

7. The claimants are also entitled for an amount of Rs.30,000/- under the conventional heads as per Heerabai W/O Kashinath Pawar And Ors vs Ramachandra Natha Sangolkar And Anr on 4 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159273833/

sentences.text: Accordingly, the claimants are entitled for total compensation of Rs.9,38,250/- as against Rs.3,93,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
There will be enhancement of Rs.5,45,250/-.

9. Relying on the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Pappu Vs. Vinod Kumar Lamba2, the respondent No.2 - Insurance Company, this Court finds it reasonable to direct respondent No.2 - Insurance Company to pay the compensation to the claimants at the (2018) 3 SCC 208 NC:
2025:KHC-K:6796 HC-KAR first instance and thereafter recover the same from respondent No.1-owner of the vehicle.

10. For the aforesaid reasons, the following:
ORDER (i) The appeal is allowed.

( ii) The appellants are entitled for total compensation of Rs.9,38,250/- with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization (excluding interest for 1417 days, the delay caused in filing the appeal).
(iii) Respondent No.2 - Insurance Company is directed to deposit the compensation amount within four weeks from the date of this judgment.
(iv) Liberty is reserved to respondent No.2 - Insurance Company to recover the same from respondent No.1.

NC: 2025:KHC-K:6796 HC-KAR (v) On such deposit, appellants Nos.2 to 5/children of the deceased are entitled for an apportionment Rs.1,00,000/- each and appellant No.1/wife is entitled for the balance amount and they are permitted to withdraw entire amount along with interest accrued on it.
Counsel for respondent No.2 is permitted to file Vakalat within two weeks.
